Ellen / Tessa — quick technical update from the on-call rotation:

What we saw (summary):
- 08:42 PDT: first error reports from Hydra; our edge observed an increase in 429s on the /v1/enrich endpoint.
- 08:50–09:25 PDT: sustained elevated 429 + 5xx rates correlated with a retry fan-out pattern from a small percentage of Hydra clients.
- 09:06 PDT: queue depth on the primary GPU pool climbed >5000 requests, leading to tail-latency spikes and subsequent 500-class responses from the runtime under backpressure.

Root cause hypothesis: sudden client-side retry amplification interacting with a pathological prefix in requests that prevented KV-cache hits, causing heavy regen-load. That combination pushed a focused set of shards beyond their processing window.

Mitigations applied:
- 09:12 PDT: enacted per-tenant throttling to cap concurrent inflight requests and reject excess with 429s (avoids runtime OOM/500s).
- 09:18 PDT: swapped Hydra traffic to a warm replica pool (lower queue depth) for 20 minutes to reduce end-user timeouts.
- 09:28 PDT: patched routing rule to spread affected prefixes across additional shards.

Next steps:
- We are compiling a tight timeline + packet-level traces; attaching an annotated incident timeline.
- We will propose a credit calculation that follows our contract methodology and also include a goodwill component for the conversion loss.

Attachments: hydra_incident_timeline.pdf, postmortem-draft.md

We will follow up with a proposed credit number and an exec call time.

—Dylan
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
